items.claim: Carlsberg Britvic announced a 10-year partnership with The Rivers Trust to restore rivers, wetlands and floodplains near its Rugby site, stating an aim to replenish 100% of the water consumed there by 2032.
items.source: Carlsberg Group newsroom release; Paul Davies, CEO of Carlsberg Britvic, quoted saying "Water is at the heart of every drink we make, so protecting this precious resource is not only important for our business, it's a responsibility we take seriously."

items.claim: Mark Lloyd said the summer was a stark reminder that water cannot be taken for granted, citing record UK temperatures and the impact of pollution and drought on rivers, in the same partnership release.
items.source: Mark Lloyd, CEO of The Rivers Trust

items.claim: 'This is an important milestone in our long-term commitment to Kazakhstan, but it is also a major step in the development of our business across Central Asia' - sagt i forbindelse med aabningen af Carlsberg Kazakhstans nye braggeri, som selskabet beskriver som et regionalt produktions- og forsyningsknudepunkt for Centralasien.
'Investments of this scale are only possible when businesses have confidence in long-term partnership and stability.'

Business Today skrev, at Carlsberg India har faaet SEBI's godkendelse af sin fortrolige IPO-ansoegning og dermed er rykket taettere paa en boersnotering, og at detaljer om stoerrelse og tidspunkt foerst kommer naar dokumenterne offentliggoeres.

Carlsberg Britvic proposed closing the Marston's Brewery in Burton upon Trent together with its primary logistics operation at the site, with closure planned for summer 2027 and further detail to follow after a consultation process.
items.source: Carlsberg Britvic, as reported by Grocery Gazette (Abigail Thakadu)

items.claim: Paul Davies said "the stark reality is that UK cask ale volumes have more than halved in less than a decade" and that "it is my role to ensure Carlsberg Britvic's multi-beverage portfolio is focused on where consumers are today".
items.source: Paul Davies, CEO of Carlsberg Britvic

items.claim: Paul Davies said of the site that "Marston's Brewery, its history and legacy in Burton upon Trent are iconic, and our teams there are true experts in ale", calling the proposal "by no means a reflection on any of our people".
items.source: Paul Davies, CEO of Carlsberg Britvic

items.claim: Carlsberg Britvic said Hobgoblin, McEwan's and Brooklyn would stay in the portfolio while other regional ale brands would be sold, with smaller brands expected to go to specialist or local ownership.
items.source: Carlsberg Britvic, as reported by Grocery Gazette

items.claim: In a letter to CAMRA, Paul Davies wrote that "this proposal does not mean that Carlsberg Britvic is withdrawing from ale", and said of the smaller ale brands that "we will do everything we can to ensure they thrive under more specialist or local ownership in the future".
items.source: Paul Davies, CEO of Carlsberg Britvic, in a letter to CAMRA, as reported by The Drinks Business

items.claim: CAMRA chairman Ash Corbett-Collins called the decision "an absolute disgrace".
Fiboinvest skriver i sit ugebrev for uge 42, at ugens rotation ud af teknologi trak investorerne mod defensive aktier, og placerer Carlsberg i den defensive gruppe blandt ugens vindere i C25.
Vietnam er et af Carlsbergs vigtigste vaekstmarkeder, og koncernens tillid til markedet bygger paa mere end tre aartiers investeringer der.
items.source: Jacob Aarup-Andersen, koncernchef (Group CEO), Carlsberg Group, i selskabets egen meddelelse

items.claim: Udvidelsen af Phu Bai-bryggeriet i Hue kaldes 'a clear demonstration of our commitment', og Carlsberg ser yderligere muligheder for at bygge videre paa det fundament.

Carlsberg oplyser at have overrakt hensigtserklaeringer (Letters of Intent) til formaendene for folkekomiteerne i Hue og Da Nang for perioden 2026-2031 og at ville udvide forretning og drift i Da Nang.
items.source: Carlsberg Group, selskabets egen meddelelse i forbindelse med Vietnams statsbesoeg i Danmark 19.-21. oktober 2026
